applicableAreas: South property boundary near southeast corner
findings.comment: Large shade trees (Cedar Elm and/or Live Oak—non-utility-compatible species per ECM Appendix F) are proposed at approximately 0 feet lateral distance from the overhead electric (OHE) conductor line running along the southern property boundary. These trees are placed directly adjacent to or underneath the OHE line, violating the 15-foot minimum clearance requirement for non-utility-compatible trees from distribution conductors. Move non-utility-compatible trees to minimum 15 feet from the outside conductor, or replace with utility-compatible species (e.g., Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud).

applicableAreas: South property boundary near southeast corner
findings.comment: Large trees with mature heights of 40+ feet (Cedar Elm and Live Oak per ECM Appendix F) are proposed at approximately 0 feet from the overhead electric distribution conductor. The 25-foot minimum clearance zone is violated. Move large trees to minimum 25 feet from the outside conductor, or select trees with mature heights less than 40 feet for this location.

applicableAreas: West of Building 2 (0.1 feet from pad-mount)
East of Building 4/North of Building 5 (2.3 feet from pad-mount)
East of Building 7/North of Building 6 (12.3 feet from pad-mount)
findings.comment: Trees are proposed within 10 lateral feet of pad-mounted electrical transformers at three locations: 0.1 feet west of Building 2, 2.3 feet east of Building 4/north of Building 5, and 12.3 feet east of Building 7/north of Building 6. All three locations violate the 10-foot minimum clearance requirement. Relocate trees to minimum 10 lateral feet from all pad-mounted equipment, ensuring they do not interfere with access doors or drivable surfaces.

applicableAreas: Landscape plan throughout, particularly near overhead electric facilities
findings.comment: Large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) cannot be verified on the landscape plans. The plant schedule on Sheet 35 lists only minimum planting heights (e.g., Live Oak and Cedar Elm at 16' minimum), not mature heights. Without mature height designations on the landscape plan or schedule, it is impossible to verify which trees will reach 40+ feet at maturity and thus require the 25-foot distribution conductor clearance. Add mature height (MH) notation to the plant schedule and differentiate large trees (MH 40+) on the landscape plan with explicit labeling.

applicableAreas: South property boundary (trees near OHE line); pad-mounted transformer locations
findings.comment: Plans propose trees within prohibited clearance zones (0 feet from OHE distribution conductors, 0.1-12.3 feet from pad-mounted equipment) without documented written approval from Austin Energy. Obtain explicit written approval from Austin Energy authorizing placement of non-compliant trees, or relocate all trees to comply with minimum clearance distances from conductors and equipment as detailed in EL-2.1, EL-2.3, and EL-2.7.
